title: Rally against police brutality, racial profiling
article: A group of protesters is marching to city hall today to protest police brutality - especially against aboriginal people.
The rally begins outside the Turtle Island Recreation Center, where in 2005 18-year-old Matthew Dumas was shot and killed by a Winnipeg police officer.
After a ceremony for Dumas and others harmed in the course of police investigations, the protesters will head to city hall for a 3 p.m. rally.
In a press release, the coalition calls Winnipeg a bastion of racial profiling, where aboriginal people are reluctant to turn to police for help.
"We demand that the City of Winnipeg provide better police services to the Indigenous community," the release states.
Indigenous Solidarity Walk & Rally To Stop Police Violence will conclude with a prayer and healing ceremony for the Winnipeg Police Service at city hall.
